# NB: the outage-test card lives in m02 only (duplicate dropped in the 26/08 cloze rewrite).
What five things does AI-free forbid?¶{{c1::Claude}} · {{c1::autocomplete/Copilot}} · {{c1::AI search summaries}} · {{c1::concept chats}} · {{c1::pasting errors in}}
column2: Allowed: docs, your own notes, help(), the REPL, paper.

column1: What are the five steps of the unassisted wall protocol?¶{{c1::Re-read the error bottom-up}} · {{c1::reproduce in the smallest snippet}} · {{c1::inspect real values}} · {{c1::one written hypothesis at a time}} · {{c1::45 min no progress = log it, return tomorrow}}
What is the honesty clause for AI-free work?¶{{c1::Log every breach — what and how long}}
column2: A quantified breach is data; a hidden one corrupts your baseline forever.

column1: Why grade your build BEFORE showing anyone?¶{{c1::Grading first forces criteria}}
column2: Grading after invites rationalising whatever you built.

column1: What makes a test worth having, and how do you prove it?¶{{c1::It would CATCH a real break}} — proven by {{c1::breaking the code on purpose and watching it fail}}
Why must errors exit non-zero?¶{{c1::Exit codes are how other programs detect failure}}
column2: A traceback is not an interface.

column1: What is the fast-track exit test, and its pass mark?¶{{c1::A cold 30-minute interview sim}} — pass = {{c1::9+/12}}
column2: Projects + Python + how LLMs work + judgement, scored 0–2 each.

column1: What does a low interview-sim score mean?¶{{c1::The gaps were found — misses become drills and cards; re-sit in a fortnight}}
column2: The trend is the instrument, not the single score.

column1: Why build a tool you'll actually use?¶{{c1::A tool you don't use taught syntax; a tool you use teaches design}}
column2: You meet your own decisions again after three days.

column1: What is module 12's most valuable artefact?¶{{c1::A wall you crossed alone}}
column2: Worth more than the finished tool.
